title: Implement global `deep_equals` function

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
![grafik](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bcbf833-5609-495b-9f0f-738d3e0f1ccc)

A deep equality check for all variant types is something I have long missed, so this PR implements it - and I'm sure I'm not the only one. (I needed to implement this for most of my projects)
Since this is an essential feature, addressing a need discussed several times in forums etc., but never formally tracked, I allowed myself to directly implement this without a proposal. Well, and while it works in GDScript, it's much slower than a native solution. In addition, implementing this yourself can be error-prone, so the goal of this PR is to provide a solid implementation that behaves expectedly.
But if a formal proposal is desired, I could create one.

Includes unit tests.

# How it works

- Compares basic types using `==` 
- Compares `Object`, `Dictionary` and `Array` recursively
	- Compares arrays element wise (like `==`)
	- Compares dictionaries order-independently
	- Compares objects by their properties (which includes metadata) order-independently

# Why another function?

## `is_same`
"Returns `true`, for value types, if `a` and `b` share the same value. Returns `true`, for reference types, if the references of `a` and `b` are the same." (quoted from docs)
(`is_same` uses the `==` operator for `Object`s, so they are compared by object ID)

## `==` and `recursive_equal`
- the `==` operator uses `Variant::hash_compare` which calls `recursive_equal` (only exposed for `Dictionary`) on `Array` and `Dictionary`, whereby `Object`s are compared by reference (object ID)
- Changing the behavior of `==` for `Object`s would be a massive compat-breakage (so we can't just modify `Variant::hash_compare`)

There is no way to do a predictable deep equality check when using the hash function (since for object two content-equal object have different hashes), so I went with a predictable and solid deep equality check

# Remarks & Discussion

~~- Should it be named something like `deep_equals` to make its purpose clearer?~~ Yes :)
